purpose: Define authenticated sessions as explicit bounded identities tied to an IAM identity and assurance evidence, separate from AccessCore permissions.

topics.name: IAM Authentication Session Identity
topics.purpose: Define authenticated sessions as explicit bounded identities tied to an IAM identity and assurance evidence, separate from AccessCore permissions.

semantics.identity_rule: Each session has an explicit session identity.
semantics.subject_rule: Session references one exact IAM identity.
semantics.lifetime_rule: Issued, expiry, idle-lifetime and renewal semantics are explicit.
semantics.channel_rule: Terminal/web/remote channel binding is explicit where required.
semantics.authorization_rule: Session proves authenticated context only; it does not itself grant AccessCore rights.
semantics.secret_rule: Session secret material is never emitted into ordinary logs/canonical JSON.

invariants.rule: Identity, authentication assurance, authorization policy, authorization decision, delegation and runtime execution remain separate machine-significant identities/evidence; no one layer silently substitutes for another.

Ambiguous, missing, stale or unverifiable authority for a protected effect fails closed rather than inheriting trust from locality, transport reachability, process ownership, UI visibility or previous success.

references.purpose: Successful authentication may create a bounded session.
